clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:
Section 1. Background. With Executive Order 14195 of February 1, 2025 
(Imposing Duties to Address the Synthetic Opioid Supply Chain in the 
People’s Republic of China), I determined that the failure of the Government 
of the People’s Republic of China (PRC) to act to blunt the sustained influx 
of synthetic opioids, including fentanyl, flowing from the PRC to the United 
States constituted an unusual and extraordinary threat, which has its source 
in substantial part outside the United States, to the national security, foreign 
policy, and economy of the United States. To address that threat, I invoked 
my authority under section 1702(a)(1)(B) of IEEPA to impose ad valorem 
tariffs on articles that are products of the PRC, as defined by the Federal 
Register notice described in section 2(d) of Executive Order 14195, as amend-
ed by Executive Order 14200 of February 5, 2025 (Amendment to Duties 
Addressing the Synthetic Opioid Supply Chain in the People’s Republic 
of China). 
Pursuant to section 3 of Executive Order 14195, I have determined that 
the PRC has not taken adequate steps to alleviate the illicit drug crisis 
through cooperative enforcement actions, and that the crisis described in 
Executive Order 14195 has not abated.

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. Amendment. In recognition of the fact that the PRC has not taken 
adequate steps to alleviate the illicit drug crisis, section 2(a) of Executive 
Order 14195 is hereby amended by striking the words ‘‘10 percent’’ and 
inserting in lieu thereof the words ‘‘20 percent’’.

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed 
to impair or otherwise affect:

clauses.label: (i)
clauses.text:
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department, agency, or 
the head thereof; or

clauses.label: (ii)
clauses.text:
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and 
subject to the availability of appropriations.

Executive Order 14228 of March 3, 2025 
Further Amendment to Duties Addressing the Synthetic 
Opioid Supply Chain in the People’s Republic of China 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including the International Emergency 
Economic Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.) (IEEPA), the National Emer-
gencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1601 et seq.), section 604 of the Trade Act of 1974, 
as amended (19 U.S.C. 2483), and section 301 of title 3, United States 
Code, I hereby determine and order: 
Section 1. Background. With Executive Order 14195 of February 1, 2025 
(Imposing Duties to Address the Synthetic Opioid Supply Chain in the 
People’s Republic of China), I determined that the failure of the Government 
of the People’s Republic of China (PRC) to act to blunt the sustained influx 
of synthetic opioids, including fentanyl, flowing from the PRC to the United 
States constituted an unusual and extraordinary threat, which has its source 
in substantial part outside the United States, to the national security, foreign 
policy, and economy of the United States. To address that threat, I invoked 
my authority under section 1702(a)(1)(B) of IEEPA to impose ad valorem 
tariffs on articles that are products of the PRC, as defined by the Federal 
Register notice described in section 2(d) of Executive Order 14195, as amend-
ed by Executive Order 14200 of February 5, 2025 (Amendment to Duties 
Addressing the Synthetic Opioid Supply Chain in the People’s Republic 
of China). 
Pursuant to section 3 of Executive Order 14195, I have determined that 
the PRC has not taken adequate steps to alleviate the illicit drug crisis 
through cooperative enforcement actions, and that the crisis described in 
Executive Order 14195 has not abated. 
Sec. 2. Amendment. In recognition of the fact that the PRC has not taken 
adequate steps to alleviate the illicit drug crisis, section 2(a) of Executive 
Order 14195 is hereby amended by striking the words ‘‘10 percent’’ and 
inserting in lieu thereof the words ‘‘20 percent’’. 
Sec. 3. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed 
to impair or otherwise affect: 
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department, agency, or 
the head thereof; or 
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals. 
(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and 
subject to the availability of appropriations.

status_research.rationale: I read the complete held EO 14228 (90 FR 11463, March 3, 2025): sec. 1 background, sec. 2 its only operative command, amending sec. 2(a) of EO 14195 (PRC synthetic-opioid tariffs) by striking '10 percent' and inserting '20 percent', and sec. 3 general provisions; no own sunset or savings clause. I read the complete held EO 14389 (91 FR 9437, Feb. 20, 2026, Ending Certain Tariff Actions). Sec. 1 says that 'the additional ad valorem duties imposed pursuant to IEEPA in ... Executive Order 14195, as amended ... shall no longer be in effect and, as soon as practicable, shall no longer be collected', sec. 2(a) directs agencies to end those duties, and sec. 2(d) confines the order to the additional IEEPA duties. The duties 'imposed ... in Executive Order 14195, as amended' include the 20 percent rate that is the whole operative content of EO 14228, so that rate no longer has effect, and EO 14228 has no other command to survive; sec. 1 preserves other actions only if they 'do not impose additional ad valorem duties'. The 'as amended' phrase reaches EO 14228 without naming it, and EO 14389 says the national emergencies remain in effect, so the basis is the termination of the duty effect, not a revocation of the order text. Residual risks: EO 14389 gives no single effective date ('as soon as practicable'); de minimis suspensions that cite EO 14228 (EO 14256, EO 14324) were examined only through the quoted passage and are separate orders; the catalog cross-references to EO 14200 and EO 14256 are not endings. The held EO 14324 ACT passages are recitals, not an ending, and are not relied on. Provisional NO hypothesis only.

reviews.rationale: I read the full held EO 14228 (90 FR 11463-11464): its only operative command (sec. 2) amends sec. 2(a) of EO 14195 to raise the IEEPA ad valorem duty on PRC products from 10 to 20 percent; no sunset or savings clause. I read the full held official FR text of EO 14389 (91 FR 9437-9439): sec. 1 provides that 'the additional ad valorem duties imposed pursuant to IEEPA in ... Executive Order 14195, as amended ... shall no longer be in effect', sec. 2(a) directs agencies to end them, and sec. 2(d) limits the order to those IEEPA duties; the national emergencies and non-duty actions are preserved, but EO 14228 has no non-duty content. The ACT: record's span was captured from an APP copy, but I verified the identical sec. 2(a) wording in the held official FR actor text ACTOR_TEXT:EO:14389, which is the text I rely on. Refutation attempt: I found in the held FR corpus EO 14357 (Nov. 4, 2025, 90 FR 50725), which expressly reduced the 20 percent rate set by EO 14228 to 10 percent effective Nov. 10, 2025; that is very probably the first end of EO 14228's operative content and the producer did not identify it (it records the first end as unresolved). That only moves the end earlier and makes the NO stronger; EO 14389 then ends whatever IEEPA duty remained under EO 14195 as amended. De minimis suspensions citing EO 14195 'as amended by EO 14228' concern the article class, which EO 14228 did not change. Independent view NO; I agree, with EO 14357 recorded as the likely first-end instrument for lifecycle work and later court rulings or reinstatements after Feb. 20, 2026 as unexamined. Nonauthoritative AI hypothesis.
